why: Part 2: no dash; plain words

why: Part 2: shorter; no dash; leads into Program the helper
old: A clear description names ALL of it: the object, the starting position, the ending position, the direction, and the path. "The toy car started at the tree, moved 3 feet in a straight path to the right, and ended at the fence" — anyone reading that could draw it.
new: A clear description names ALL of it: where it started, which way it went, its path and where it ended. Sam’s delivery robot, Scoot, will test your descriptions. Scoot does exactly what your words say.

why: plain words: “misconception” is a hard word; no dashes; same idea
old: Common misconception: Some people think motion is something an object "has." Motion is actually a COMPARISON — it only exists relative to a reference point. The same object can be at rest AND in motion at the same time, just compared to different things.
new: Watch out: some people think an object is either moving or not, and that’s that. But motion is a COMPARISON. On the train, you were at rest compared to your seat and in motion compared to the station sign, both at once.
